name: Fort Douaumont
significance: Primary objective - largest fort in Verdun defensive system
notes: Lost to Germans Feb 25 after minimal resistance; recaptured Oct 24 after massive bombardment

name: Fort Vaux
significance: Major defensive position - scene of 7-day siege
notes: Heroic defense May 31-Jun 7; garrison held despite no water; recaptured Nov 2 after German evacuation

name: Fort Souville
notes: German high-water mark; never captured by Germans

name: Fort Tavannes
significance: Tunnel fort - underground shelter and supply depot
notes: Major tunnel system; site of ammunition explosion May 4

name: Fort Thiaumont
significance: Contested position between Douaumont and Fleury

name: Mort-Homme (Hill 295)
significance: Key Left Bank position - brutal fighting March-May
notes: The Dead Man - changed hands multiple times

name: Hill 304
notes: Named for elevation; critical for observing French lines

name: Fleury-devant-Douaumont
significance: Village destroyed and recaptured multiple times
notes: Changed hands 16 times; completely destroyed; "village that died for France"

name: Douaumont village
notes: Captured same day as fort; never rebuilt

name: Beaumont
significance: Village captured early in German offensive
notes: One of first villages to fall

name: Ornes
notes: Zone Rouge (Red Zone) after war; never rebuilt

name: Vaux-devant-Damloup
notes: Captured by French Nov 3 after Vaux recapture

name: Haumont
notes: First village destroyed; "disappeared from the map"

name: Bois des Caures
significance: Forest - site of initial German assault
notes: Col. Driant's defense; first day of battle

name: Meuse River
notes: Natural barrier; crossed by bridges at Verdun

name: Tunnel de Tavannes
significance: Underground tunnel system at Fort Tavannes
notes: Housed thousands of soldiers; site of May 4 explosion (500+ killed)

name: Voie Sacrée (Sacred Way)
significance: Supply road from Bar-le-Duc to Verdun (75km)
notes: Lifeline of Verdun; 3,000 trucks/day; one vehicle every 14 seconds

name: Bar-le-Duc
notes: Main supply hub for Verdun operations

name: R1 Trench
significance: Main French trench line near Douaumont

name: German High-Water Mark (Jun 23)
notes: After this date French counteroffensives begin reversing gains

name: French Front Line (Dec 18)
significance: French line at battle end Dec 18 1916
notes: Restored to near Feb 21 positions; Germans lost nearly all gains

name: Observation Post - Mort-Homme
notes: After capture commanded view of Verdun

name: Battery Position - Azannes
notes: Fired on Verdun city and rear areas

name: Battlefield Center
significance: Approximate geographic center of combat zone

name: Right Bank Zone
notes: 35 km² combat zone; majority of casualties

name: Left Bank Zone
notes: 25 km² combat zone; fierce fighting Mar-May

name: No-Man's-Land (typical)
notes: Width: 50-500 meters depending on sector; instant death zone

name: Zone Rouge (Red Zone)
significance: Post-war exclusion zone - too dangerous for habitation
notes: 100+ km² still restricted today; unexploded ordnance, soil contamination

name: Citadel of Verdun
notes: Housed 1000s of troops; command center; hospital

name: Dugny
notes: Supply depot for Left Bank operations
